result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as test code (mock resources), whatever follows it. The new test passes (3 tests, 0 failures). I did not commit.

**What changed**
- `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`: the two mock-folder conventions in `addTestConventions()` now use `[^/]*` instead of `[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+`:
  - `.*/__mock[^/]*/.*`
  - `.*/mock[^/]*/.*`
  
  The `[^/]*` keeps the match inside one folder name, so `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/` and files named `mock.java` or `mockery.java` still don't match. The existing backslash handling in `SourceFileFilter` covers Windows paths.
- New test `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsMockFoldersTest.java` covers:
  - the new cases: plain `mock/` (including the elasticsearch path), `mock.data`, `mock(old)`, `mock-größe`, `mock模拟`, `__mock/`, nested and backslash paths;
  - the previously matched folders (`mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/`, `mockStore/`);
  - the non-matches (`remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java`, `mockery.java`).

I didn't run the full module test suite, only the new test class.
